implementation.name: SMS (MiSTer)
implementation.notes: Source availability (T5.4): open -- the repository carries 60 HDL source files (9 systemverilog, 11 verilog, 40 vhdl) alongside 35 prebuilt .rbf binaries. There is no open_source column in the delivered schema (data-model.md §1.9 deleted the proposed core table together with its flags); the presence of hdl_language_id and of implementation_path rows is how that fact is stated here. Machine mapping: hand-mapped, not MRA-setname-derived -- a console core ships no MRA files. The core reimplements the Sega Master System and the Game Gear: the distribution's _Console/Game Gear.mgl names <rbf>_Console/SMS</rbf>, and GameGear2P is a second build of this same repository, giving machine_id sms and machine_id gamegear. Every id was checked against extract/machine.json. This console core doubles as an arcade core: Machine mapping: 9 arcade MRA files in Distribution_MiSTer/_Arcade naming <rbf>SMS</rbf> carry a <setname>; 8 resolved exactly to a MAME 0.288 machine and 1 through MAME's own cloneof relation to the parent set that survives extract/machine.json's parents-only filter, giving 8 distinct machine_id rows. Those setnames are MAME shortnames, so this part of the mapping is setname-derived. License: the repository has no LICENSE, COPYING or COPYRIGHT file; the grant lives in the source header at https://github.com/MiSTer-devel/SMS_MiSTer/blob/master/SMS.sv, which offers the work under the GNU General Public License "either version 2 of the License, or (at your option) any later version" -- hence GPL-2.0-or-later. hdl_language_id: no single HDL family reaches 90% of the 60 source files (9 systemverilog, 11 verilog, 40 vhdl), excluding the shared framework directory. accuracy_id omitted: the repository makes no timing-fidelity claim this build could verify.
